title: India's DPDP Act for everyone at work
summary: What the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 means for your day-to-day work.
body_md:
## What the law covers

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) and the DPDP Rules, 2025 govern **digital personal data**:
any data in digital form about an individual who can be identified by or from it. Names, phone numbers, email
addresses, Aadhaar and PAN numbers, device IDs and account histories are all personal data.

The person the data is about is the **Data Principal**. Our company decides why and how the data is processed,
which makes us a **Data Fiduciary**. Vendors who process data on our behalf are **Data Processors**, and we stay
responsible for what they do.

## The core rules

1. **A lawful reason.** We process personal data only with the person's consent or for a "legitimate use" listed
   in Section 7 of the Act, such as employment purposes or a legal obligation.
2. **Clear notice.** When we ask for consent, we explain in plain language what data we collect and why.
3. **Only what's needed.** Collect and use only the data required for the stated purpose.
4. **Keep it accurate and safe.** Protect data with reasonable security safeguards.
5. **Delete when done.** Erase data when the purpose is complete or consent is withdrawn, unless the law requires
   us to keep it.

## Rights of Data Principals

People can ask us for a summary of their data, ask us to correct or erase it, withdraw consent, nominate someone
to act for them, and raise a grievance. Grievances must be answered within the period set by the Rules (no more
than 90 days), and our internal target is shorter.

**If a customer asks you about their data, don't handle it informally.** Log it as a rights request or send them
to our privacy request page so it gets tracked and answered on time.

## Children's data

Processing the data of anyone under 18 needs verifiable consent from a parent or guardian. Tracking, behavioural
monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children are not allowed.

## Personal data breaches

If personal data is lost, leaked, accessed without authorisation or made unavailable, it's a personal data
breach. We must inform the Data Protection Board and affected people without delay, and send the Board a detailed
report within 72 hours. Report anything you suspect to the security team **immediately**; don't investigate on
your own.

## Penalties

Failing to take reasonable security safeguards can lead to penalties of up to ₹250 crore per instance. Most
breaches come from everyday mistakes, which is why every one of us matters.

quiz.q: Which of these is personal data under the DPDP Act?
options: A customer's phone number stored in our CRM
Our office electricity bill
Anonymous, aggregated website traffic totals
The source code of our app

quiz.q: A customer emails you asking us to delete their account data. What should you do?
options: Delete it yourself straight away from the database
Ignore it unless they ask again
Log it as a rights request (or point them to our privacy request page) so it is tracked and answered in time
Tell them deletion isn't possible

quiz.q: Within how long must the detailed breach report reach the Data Protection Board?
options: 6 hours
72 hours
30 days
Only if more than 1,000 people are affected

quiz.q: What's needed before processing personal data of a 15-year-old?
options: Nothing special
The child's own consent
Verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian
Approval from the Data Protection Board

quiz.q: Who is responsible when a vendor that processes data for us has a breach?
options: Only the vendor
Our company remains responsible as the Data Fiduciary
Nobody, because it happened outside our systems
The Data Principal
